title: Sonic Adventure 2
subtitle: Two sides of the same race
summary: Sonic and Shadow lead parallel campaigns that alternate fast platforming, mechanical shooting and treasure hunting.
body: Sonic Adventure 2 is Sonic Team USA’s three-dimensional platform adventure, first released for Dreamcast in North America on 19 June 2001. Its Hero and Dark campaigns follow the same crisis from opposing sides. Sonic, Tails and Knuckles face Shadow, Doctor Eggman and Rouge, with the story eventually bringing their journeys together. Each side has a runner, a machine pilot and a treasure hunter. Moving between those roles changes the task as well as the character, making the campaign a succession of distinct kinds of stage.

Sonic and Shadow race through platforming courses, using homing attacks and grinding along rails. Tails and Eggman pilot armed machines, locking onto targets as they work through more deliberate shooting stages. Knuckles and Rouge search larger spaces for hidden objects, using radar and clues to narrow the search. The campaigns repeatedly return to these three patterns, so players learn related abilities on both sides of the story. Outside the missions, animals and items collected along the way can be taken into the Chao gardens.

Sonic Team USA developed the game around its American surroundings, with San Francisco among the influences on the urban stages. City Escape opens with Sonic descending city streets before the route turns into a pursuit. The music gives the cast equally distinct identities, ranging from rock to rap and orchestral passages. Jun Senoue, Fumie Kumatani, Tomoya Ohtani and Kenichi Tokoi contributed to the score. Released around Sonic’s tenth anniversary, the game became his final new adventure made for a Sega console before its later adaptations.
story_headings: A city with its own rhythm
